channel.title: PDX Spend
channel.description: Seven voter-passed funds in Portland and Multnomah County, quietly redrawn around their balances. An editorial accounting of restricted public funds.

item.title: PDX Spend, Issue 01
item.description: Seven voter-passed funds in Portland and Multnomah County have been quietly redrawn around their balances.

item.title: Cross-fund dashboard
item.description: Three views of all seven funds: dollars, share-restricted, and drift trajectory.

item.title: Generate a structured financial memo
item.description: Pick a fund and a lens; the agent re-runs the memo against the modeled record.

item.title: Methodology
item.description: How this site was built: what is modeled, why, and how audited figures will be swapped in.

item.title: Implications
item.description: What the seven funds, taken together, suggest about the structural pattern.

item.title: Arts Education and Access Fund
item.description: A flat tax billed as a teacher-funding measure spends roughly one in eight dollars on the cost of collecting itself, and Council periodically expands what counts as "arts."

item.title: Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund
item.description: A surcharge passed for clean energy and BIPOC workforce now backfills street paving and parks budgets after Council expanded "eligible uses" by simple majority.

item.title: Housing Investment Fund (TIF Set-Aside)
item.description: A 30% set-aside policy has been re-engineered through reclassification: projects counted as "affordable" include workforce-grade and market-rate-with-amenities developments.

item.title: Rental Services / Tenant Protections Fund
item.description: A landlord-paid fund for tenant services consistently spends less than half its inflow on tenant services, with the remainder absorbed into housing-bureau overhead.

item.title: Metro Affordable Housing Bond
item.description: A 3,900-home bond is on track to deliver fewer homes per dollar than promised; jurisdictions have re-classified "preservation" of existing units to keep count metrics intact.

item.title: Preschool For All
item.description: A tuition-free preschool tax has built a half-billion-dollar surplus while serving a fraction of the eligible 3- and 4-year-olds the measure was designed to cover.

item.title: Supportive Housing Services Measure
item.description: A homelessness measure has accumulated a multi-hundred-million dollar reserve while service contracts go unfilled and rent assistance waitlists grow.
